verdict.rationale: Orb's hosted first-party MCP server exposes 100+ API operations covering subscriptions, plans and credits, so an agent can make subscription changes. It acts with the connected key's permissions, and key scopes are set per area to none, read or write. The API itself also documents subscription creation, plan changes and edits, and test-mode keys isolate experimentation from live billing data. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of an agent performing these operations under scoped keys, and an explicit documented credit-grant endpoint (credits are covered only within the MCP tool listing).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can operate my billing — create a subscription, apply a credit, change a plan — through a programmatic surface with scoped permissions

citations.quote: It exposes 100+ Orb API operations as tools, covering customers, subscriptions, plans and prices, billable metrics, invoices, credits, alerts, licenses, event search and price evaluation
Each scope covers one area of Orb... and can be set to **none**, **read** or **write**
You can create a subscription either from the Orb UI or via the subscription creation API endpoint.
When you change plans, the subscription ID remains the same, but Orb maintains a complete audit trail of every plan assignment.
To try things out without touching live billing data, create the key in **test mode**.
